articles.title: Bird flu fears prompt orders for farmers to keep poultry inside in England and Scotland
articles.summary:
Increased risk of devastating strain means restrictions imposed for second year in a row on those keeping birds

Poultry and captive birds across England and Scotland must be kept inside for…

blocks.text: Poultry and captive birds across England and Scotland must be kept inside for the second year in a row due to an increased risk of a devastating strain of bird flu.

The British government has issued an England-wide avian influenza prevention zone, meaning individuals with 50 or more poultry or captive birds must house them inside. A similar designation was made across the whole of Scotland on Tuesday.
Birdkeepers must also follow enhanced biosecurity measures including reporting changes in egg production and reporting suspected disease immediately to the Animal and Plant Health Agency.
The government said the declaration followed an increased risk and escalating number of confirmations of the highly pathogenic avian influenza, or bird flu, in kept and wild birds.
A prevention zone was also declared across all of England, Scotland and Wales in 2025.

The disease has been spreading rapidly since 2014 and has devastated UK wild bird populations since the summer of 2021. It has also spread across an unusually broad range of species around the world, including in four of the five main southern elephant seal populations. In some south Atlantic colonies, more than 90% of newborn pups have died, alongside about half of all adult females.
The disease has also been detected in humans, with 11 deaths recorded globally between 1 January and 4 August 2025.
This strain of bird flu causes illness and high death rates in birds, and flu-like symptoms and conjunctivitis in humans who come into close contact with infected animals.
The British government said the current risk to human health from bird flu remained very low.

The government says it does not anticipate an impact on the availability of Christmas turkeys or other seasonal poultry for consumers. The Food Safety Authority said properly cooked poultry and poultry products, including eggs, were safe to eat.

The UK chief veterinary officer, Christine Middlemiss, said: “Having avian influenza confirmed in your flock can be devastating. I understand the impact this disease can have on the poultry sector and am extremely grateful for the continued cooperation of the industry.”

articles.title: New Orleans attorney fined $400,000 after exposing abusive priest says it was ‘worth it’
articles.summary:
Richard Trahant says accusers have been vindicated after Catholic church officially classifies Paul Hart as sex abuser

An attorney who was
articles.byline: Ramon Antonio Vargas in New Orleans

blocks.text: An attorney who was fined more than $400,000 after getting an abusive Roman Catholic priest removed as a New Orleans high school’s chaplain says it was “worth it” now that the church has officially classified the cleric as a clergy molester.

That remark from Richard Trahant came days after the archdiocese of New Orleans, having waited years, added Paul Hart on 6 November to a list of Catholic priests and deacons faced with credible claims of clergy abuse while serving in the area.

The late Hart had previously dismissed news coverage of his admitted but largely unpunished sexual misconduct with a 17-year-old girl he met in the course of his ministry as “bogus” and “made-up”. But, while continuing to implement the terms of an agreement to settle a bankruptcy protection case that it filed amid the fallout of the Catholic church’s worldwide clergy abuse scandal, the New Orleans archdiocese ultimately included Hart on a list of more than 100 credibly accused priests and deacons – vindicating those who spoke out against him and his religious superiors.
“This is the very definition of a Pyrrhic victory,” Trahant said, invoking a phrase for something achieved at a high cost. “Sure, it’s exoneration – yet only after I paid a fortune.
“But if the question is: was it worth it? The answer is yes, and I would do it again tomorrow.”
Hart and Trahant were at the center of one of the most contentious chapters of the New Orleans archdiocese’s bankruptcy, which the institution filed in 2020.

Trahant’s work representing clergy abuse claimants whose cases became ensnared in the archdiocesan bankruptcy gave him access to documents chronicling how Hart had secretly admitted to his supervisors that he had sexual contact with a 17-year-old girl in the early 1990s after meeting her through his role as a priest.

In 2012, she reported Hart to the church for that behavior and confessed to it during a confidential internal investigation, according to hundreds of legal documents obtained and reviewed by the Guardian.

An advisory board working with New Orleans’s archbishop at the time, Gregory Aymond, recommended removing Hart from public ministry, saying the case victimized someone who was considered a minor under canon – or church – law since 2002.
But Aymond let Hart continue his ministry because in the early 1990s the age of consent under canon law was 16. And Louisiana law sets the age of consent at 17.
Aymond then appointed Hart to serve as chaplain at Brother Martin after the New Orleans Catholic high school asked for one in 2017.

“Please know that I not only appreciate your ministry but will pray for you that God will use you to be a sign of pastoral care to our young people,” Aymond wrote to Hart after appointing him to Brother Martin, an all boys’ school where there are activities that girls can participate in.

Hart was still in that role toward the end of 2021 when Trahant became aware of his past. He notified Brother Martin’s principal – coincidentally, Trahant’s cousin – that Hart had “a credible allegation from [his] past that involved a minor”.

Also, Trahant emailed this journalist to keep Hart on his “radar”. But he would not elaborate to either Gallagher or this journalist, citing a bankruptcy court confidentiality order, according to the legal documents stemming from the case.

Aymond and the archdiocese soon provided Brother Martin with the details about Hart’s past misconduct. And he retired in January 2022, nine months before his death, after Brother Martin requested that Aymond remove him from its campus.

Meanwhile, using methods and sources exclusive of Trahant, this journalist wrote an article in New Orleans’s Times-Picayune newspaper detailing the circumstances of Hart’s departure – though the archdiocese insisted the priest had retired because of “struggles with treatment for brain cancer”.

The federal judge in charge of the archdiocese’s bankruptcy, Meredith Grabill, later ruled what Trahant had done set off a chain of events that was enough to constitute a confidentiality order violation. She fined him $400,000 – which eventually grew by $60,000 because of interest. And she expelled four of Trahant’s clients from a committee of clergy abuse survivors helping negotiate an archdiocesan bankruptcy settlement, contending that it would aid the group’s functioning.

Grabill so acted despite a court investigation which she ordered having determined that Brother Martin got the specifics about what Hart had done from the archdiocese – not Trahant, according to documents obtained by the Guardian.
Court investigators also conceded there was evidence supporting Trahant’s denial that he ever provided any confidential information to this journalist.

Trahant unsuccessfully appealed his fine from Grabill up to the US supreme court. But the supreme court declined to hear his case in June, months after Aymond’s retirement as New Orleans archbishop – so he paid the levy.

Aymond’s successor, archbishop James Checchio, on 6 November then added 27 priests and deacons to a list of credibly accused clergymen which the New Orleans archdiocese first released in 2018, calling it a step toward “accountability and healing”. The list now had 106 names after the update – a key provision of an agreement announced in December 2025 requiring the archdiocese and its insurers to eventually pay $305m to hundreds of clergy abuse survivors to resolve the bankruptcy.
Hart’s name being listed immediately leapt out at Trahant, he said.

The archdiocese said that records associated with Hart and all others on the credibly accused list would be kept at a public archive hosted by Louisiana State University. A release of such records for Hart would mean none of the information in them was ever confidential, according to Trahant.

Trahant also said he interpreted Hart’s inclusion on the credibly accused list – and a notation that he had three claims filed against him in the bankruptcy – as an admission that archdiocese and court officials had mishandled his case. Furthermore, he said it was perhaps the ultimate repudiation of one of Hart’s last known statements – telling bankruptcy court investigators that news media reporting on his departure from Brother Martin was “so bogus that it looked … almost made up”.

“He was lying,” said Trahant, mentioning that he is contemplating seeking further legal action out of principle to attempt to recoup his fine and the costs he incurred fighting it. “And … now they’ve admitted [it].”

Separately, one of the Trahant clients who was ousted from the bankruptcy settlement committee said Checchio could “truly” promote accountability by apologizing to the advocate and returning the fine money to him.
“At least [now], everyone knows that we were wrongly removed,” James Adams said. “The court sanctioned an innocent lawyer and his clients.”

articles.title: AI datacentres plan on-site power stations on huge scale despite climate risks, research reveals
articles.summary:
181GW of gas-fired capacity proposed for sites in US and Europe because of delays in connecting to national grids, says report

Developers of AI datacentres plan to build on-site…

blocks.text: Developers of AI datacentres plan to build on-site climate-destroying gas power stations on a huge scale to meet their energy demands, research reveals.

Datacentres planned across the US, the UK and mainland Europe have proposals to build fossil fuel plants on-site to create 181GW of gas-fired capacity because of delays to connect to national grids, according to the findings. This is almost four times the total peak electricity demand of Great Britain.

The research by BloombergNEF says this “speed to power” will – if the planned rollout happens – emit about 345m metric tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent a year in the US, where 90% of on-site gas-fired power stations are planned. This is equivalent to annual greenhouse gas emissions from about 72.8m fossil fuel cars.

The report was published on Wednesday as global leaders gathered in Turkey for the 31st UN climate summit, where increasing electrification – ideally from clean sources – is a central part of discussions. However, a number of key European leaders, including from France and Germany, will not be at Cop31, instead heading to Dublin where EU leaders will hold their first dedicated AI summit on Friday.

Mark Daly, the head of datacentres and emerging tech at BloombergNEF, said: “The extraordinary economics around AI are making speed to power one of the most important priorities for defining constraints on datacentre developers.

“The climate outcome will depend not only on how much electricity these facilities use, but on how quickly grids can connect them and whether power systems add cleaner generation alongside that demand.”
By 2035, the electricity demand of AI datacentres was predicted to almost quadruple to 2,354 terawatt-hours – equivalent to 7% of global electricity demand – the report said.
AI datacentres use a massive amount of electricity to power servers and cool equipment, and to run facility systems.

Daly said while the developers of the future datacentres claimed their gas-fired power supplies would be temporary while they waited for grid connections, once they were online, the economics could encourage them to continue generating energy, creating a longer-term fossil-fuel lock-in risk.

The report said ensuring new datacentres were connected to the grid was the more sustainable option. Faster grid connections were crucial to limiting emissions impacts and locking in fossil fuel risk, it said.

UK planned datacentres made more than 100 inquiries in 2024-5 to connect to gas as a result of delays in securing access to the electricity grid, according to Future Energy Networks, the representative body for the UK gas networks.
after newsletter promotion

For example, Wapseys Wood, Buckinghamshire and Quest Park, Bedfordshire are seeking to build their own on-site gas-fired power stations because of the long wait to connect to the grid. The datacentres are among the first to be fast-tracked through the government’s nationally significant infrastructure project regime, which allows developers to rapidly deliver major infrastructure, bypassing locally elected planning authorities.

But the use of fossil fuel power generation on site is likely to be repeated by many more UK sites after the chancellor, John Healey, gave the green light for datacentres to build and run temporary on-site fossil fuel power stations while they wait for connections to the grid, as part of a so-called datacentre covenant.

Oliver Hayes, the head of policy and campaigns at Global Action Plan , said: “Private gas power stations for datacentres should be a red line for any government serious about climate action, so it’s shocking to see the chancellor give them his explicit backing.
“No one seriously believes these gas power stations will be temporary – once they’re built, they’ll lock in high emissions for years.”

articles.title: Sherwin Gatchalian flags GenCorp 'conflict of interest' over Sara Duterte payouts
articles.summary: Senator-judge and Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian on Wednesday raised a possible conflict of interest after GenCorp Industries Inc. paid Vice President Sara Duterte P2.14 million as returns of…

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 7:58pm

Senator-judge and Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian on Wednesday raised a possible conflict of interest after GenCorp Industries Inc. paid Vice President Sara Duterte P2.14 million as supposed returns of capital while the company held several contracts with the Davao City government.

Gatchalian raised the issue during his interpellation of lawyer Suzette Balucanag-Punay, the in-house counsel of GenCorp and Metro City Chow Foods Corp., two companies linked to the Vice President, during the 42nd day of Duterte’s impeachment trial.
“Lumalabas ito sa kaha ng GenCorp. Tapos ang GenCorp, sa mga huling hearing, nagbebenta rin po ng pagkain sa Davao LGU (local government unit), 19 contracts between 2022 to 2025,” Gatchalian said.
(This payments came out of GenCorp.’s coffers. GenCorp., as revealed in previous hearings, also sold food to the Davao City government under 19 contracts from 2022 to 2025.)

“Tingin niyo hindi ba ito conflict of interest na ang GenCorp nagbabayad ng investment, loose investment kay Vice President Sara, pero sa kabilang banda, nagbebenta naman siya sa Davao LGU?” he asked.
(Don’t you think this is a conflict of interest, with GenCorp. paying Vice President Sara for her loose investment while also selling food to the Davao City government?)
Duterte’s brother, Sebastian “Baste” Duterte, is the incumbent Davao City mayor. The Vice President also previously served as the city’s mayor.
In response, Punay said the Davao City government contracts were fulfilled by GenCorp.’s Jollibee Bolton branch, the outlet nearest city hall, and not the branch where Duterte had her investment.
She explained that although GenCorp. owns the Bolton branch, Duterte’s "loose investment" was in the Jollibee Times Square branch. Each branch, she added, maintains a separate bank account.
Gatchalian, however, maintained that GenCorp. was still the entity making payments to the Vice President.
“So mukhang conflict of interest… Dahil sa kabilang banda, ‘yung investment binabayaran, ‘yung kita sa investment. Sa kabilang banda naman, nagbebenta ng pagkain sa Davao LGU,” he said.
(So it appears to be a conflict of interest because, on one hand, the returns on the investment are being paid, while on the other, the company is selling food to the Davao City government.)
Punay maintained that there was no conflict of interest.
“To my understanding, there's no conflict of interest because VP Sara is not part of the LGU,” she said.
Gatchalian countered that Duterte and the Davao City mayor are siblings.
Earlier in the hearing, Punay testified that Duterte had a “loose investment” in GenCorp, from which she received P2.14 million in returns of capital from 2022 to 2025.
The amount was significantly lower than the P212 million in alleged returns earlier presented by prosecution witness and financial forensic expert Alex Cabrera.

Duterte’s 2024 and 2025 Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth, which she jointly filed with her husband, Manases Carpio, were earlier presented by the prosecution as evidence of her business interests.
The documents listed GenCorp, formerly known as Times Square Bee Foods Corp. and Great Jolly Times Food, among her business interests.
Baste Duterte previously testified that the Davao City government had awarded P33 million worth of contracts to GenCorp.
He also said he was unaware that his sister had a business interest in the company.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Nvidia hires leading US law firm to investigate Jensen Huang’s relationship
articles.summary: Move comes as chipmaker reels from reports its CEO was having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy

blocks.text: Nvidia has appointed a leading US law firm to conduct a “thorough and independent” investigation into the relationship between its chief executive, Jensen Huang, and an alleged Chinese spy.

The $4.1tn (£3tn) chipmaker has hired New York-based Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz for the investigation, which will be led by the Wachtell partner Joon Kim. Wachtell’s website describes Kim, a former government prosecutor in New York, as a specialist in areas including internal investigations, white-collar criminal and regulatory defence, and crisis management.
Nvidia did not give a timeframe for the investigation but the company has said Huang will continue to lead the business he co-founded “without interruption”.
The company is reeling from an espionage scandal after reports that its chief executive had been having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, who was also an Nvidia customer.
The US ambassador to China, David Perdue, said: “The situation with Nvidia is another reminder that we have to stay diligent.
“National security is part of this economic conversation because economic security is national security. And so, what we’re doing with China is bumpy right now,” he told Bloomberg Television.

Nvidia had at first denied an improper relationship with the Chinese citizen, who is no relation to the Nvidia boss, but Huang then admitted on Sunday he had been unfaithful to his wife – without referring directly to Ms Huang.

On the same day Nvidia announced an investigation into reports that Huang “has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”. The scandal has wiped $430bn off Nvidia’s value as shareholders gauge the potential impact of the scandal on a company and an executive who are synonymous with the AI boom.

Wachtell is one of the most prestigious corporate law firms in the US. Its founding partner Martin Lipton invented the “poison pill defence” in the 1980s, a corporate gambit that helps companies ward off hostile takeovers.

Technically called the “shareholder rights plan”, the poison pill allowed investors to buy more shares at a discount if one shareholder acquired a certain percentage of the company’s stock. This made it harder for corporate raiders to acquire a company without the board’s approval.

The firm was closely involved in the takeover of Getty Oil by Texaco. This was the largest corporate takeover in history at the time, although it turned sour when the thwarted suitor Pennzoil sued Texaco and won.
In 2008, a team of Wachtell lawyers advised the US Treasury department on the takeover of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac during the financial crisis.

The company was founded in the 1960s and is said to be the most profitable law firm in the US. It pulled in revenues of $5.1m per lawyer last year and made profits of $12m per partner, the highest profits per partner ever, according to the Am Law 100 rankings.

From 2017 to 2018, Kim was the acting US attorney for the southern district of New York, where he ran a team of lawyers investigating securities and commodities fraud, mail and wire fraud, public and private corruption, money laundering, cybercrime, and tax offences.
after newsletter promotion
That included the case of the former US representative Anthony Weiner, who was sentenced to 21 months in prison for sending obscene material to a minor.
He also oversaw the prosecution of the banker Mehmet Hakan Atilla, who was convicted in 2017 of helping to evade US sanctions on Iran.
Another high-profile assignment landed on Kim’s desk in 2021, when he investigated multiple allegations of sexual harassment by the then New York governor, Andrew Cuomo.
One analyst has put Huang’s chances of leaving Nvidia at 15%.

“Right now the Street and investor chatter is assigning roughly a 15% chance he is removed as CEO of Nvidia with a high probability (85%) he stays on as CEO after the board investigation is completed,” wrote the tech analyst Dan Ives in a note to investors. “We would expect a board investigation that could take four weeks to six weeks and will create a clear overhang on the stock until more news emerges from Nvidia.”

Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, the senior associate dean for leadership studies at the Yale School of Management and the founder of the Chief Executive Leadership Institute, has put Huang’s survival chances at “about 50-50”.

articles.title: Transport workers in Chile block highways in protest over surging fuel prices
articles.summary: Hundreds of bus and lorry drivers are blocking traffic along major highway routes across the country.

blocks.text: Hundreds of transport workers in Chile have blocked roads and highways across the country in protest over high fuel prices.
Drivers of busses and lorries began protesting on Tuesday, gathering in convoys to halt traffic along major routes.
They are demanding a relief from surging diesel prices, which have been driven up by the war in Iran.
Talks between government officials and protest leaders have so far failed to reach a resolution, with another meeting expected to take place on Wednesday.
The protest is being organised by the ⁠Fuerza del Norte trade union, which represents around 80% of Chile's lorry drivers, and the No+TAG civic protest ​movement.

"There is no point of agreement with the government that could offer any perspective to find solutions for everyone," Andrés Alarcón, a spokesman for No+TAG, said after talks broke down on Tuesday, adding "the strike continues".
Economy Minister Daniel Mas called for further dialogue, but warned "at some point, we will have to clear the highways".
He stressed the protests were impacting economic activity and exports, saying "we need to get the country moving again".
The government of President José Antonio Kast has faced public discontent over fuel prices for months.
The average price of diesel has risen 74% since March, according to industry groups.
Juan Cornejo, the president of the Association of Intercity Bus Owners, which represents 14 mid-sized companies, told AFP that "we've reached our limit".
"We've spent more than a month working with negative numbers," he added.
Lorry driver Claudio Elguezabal, who took part in a protest near the capital, Santiago, on Tuesday morning, said the situation was unsustainable.
"Right now I'm not making any profit. Sometimes you even have to put in your own money to cover the client," AFP quoted the 47-year-old as saying.

articles.title: Donald Trump's ASEAN attendance set for November 17
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump is set to attend the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit on November 17, joining several other world leaders in Pasay City, Philippines, according to the…

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 7:34pm

US President Donald Trump is set to attend the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit on November 17, joining several other world leaders in Pasay City, Philippines, according to the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Wednesday.
The DFA said that the leaders and delegates from around the world will travel to the Philippines from November 16 to 18, with the opening ceremony of the ASEAN Summit to be held on November 15.
From November 16 to 17, the DFA said that the government will hold Related Summits or the Plus One Summits.

“On 17 November, the President will also convene the 29th ASEAN Plus Three Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit, the premier Leaders-led forum for dialogue and cooperation on strategic, political and economic issues of common concern and interest in the region,” the DFA said.

“The President will also lead the Closing Ceremony and the handover of the ASEAN Chairship to Singapore. The day will culminate with the ASEAN-United States Special Summit to be attended by U.S. President Donald J. Trump,” the agency added.

Leaders from other ASEAN nations are also expected to attend, namely Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Lao PDR, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, and Viet Nam. Myanmar will be represented by its ASEAN Affairs Department Director-General.
There will also be remarks from Brazilian and Canadian leaders, as well as the International Monetary Fund. They are deemed as “Guests of the Chair”.

“As the Philippines brings together ASEAN Leaders and Dialogue Partners from across the region and the wider international community, the country looks forward to engagements that will reinforce the value of dialogue, deepen partnerships, and strengthen collective responses to shared challenges,” the DFA said.
Trump’s attendance has raised concerns among several civil society groups, with many announcing protests to denounce his visit to the Philippines. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Joining lawsuit, Kennedy family members say Trump's arch would be 'denigration' of JFK, RFK plots at Arlington
articles.summary: Nine family members of the Kennedy political dynasty are asking a judge to block U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to build a towering memorial arch, saying the 76-metre structure would cast a…

image.caption: Tourists visit the gravesite of former U.S. president John F. Kennedy at Arlington National Cemetery in Arlington, Va., in a 2013 file photo. (Jewel Samad/AFP/Getty Images)

blocks.text: World·New

Nine family members of the Kennedy political dynasty are asking a judge to block U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to build a towering memorial arch, saying the 76-metre structure would cast a shadow over their relatives' gravesites at Arlington National Cemetery.
Legal filing comes with Trump administration eager to break ground on temporarily blocked project

Nine family members of the Kennedy political dynasty asked a judge on Tuesday to block U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to build a towering memorial arch, saying the 250-foot (76-metre) structure would cast a shadow over their relatives' gravesites at Arlington National Cemetery.

The shadow would "fundamentally alter the experience of visiting the gravesites," the relatives argued. They filed a motion to intervene in two existing lawsuits seeking to block construction of the arch.
U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan last week prohibited the Trump administration from breaking ground on the structure for 14 days.

The nine Kennedy family members who filed suit are children and grandchildren of Robert F. Kennedy and Edward M. Kennedy, brothers of the slain U.S. president John F. Kennedy, both of whom served in the U.S. Senate. They are buried close to the eternal flame that marks JFK's gravesite, a trio of memorials that are a major draw for the millions of people who visit the Arlington cemetery each year.
Sen. Tammy Duckworth, of Illinois, speaks at a demonstration against U.S. President Donald Trump's proposed arch on Oct. 1 in Washington. (Kylie Cooper/Reuters)
Building the arch would be a "permanent denigration" of the gravesites, lawyers for the relatives wrote.
"The Arch would significantly damage the memorial to the Kennedys, as well as the heroes who eternally rest at Arlington National Cemetery," the filing said.

"It is unfortunate to see that some members of the Kennedy family have joined the litigation against the Arch, as the project is intended to honour our heroes who rest in Arlington Cemetery," said White House spokesperson Davis Ingle. "The judiciary should not be abused to politicize a structure designed to unite our nation."
Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Trump's health and human services secretary, who has a fractured relationship with many of his relatives, did not join the lawsuit.
LISTEN | Our CBC Washington correspondents look ahead to next Congress session:
Two Blocks from the White House31:02The U.S. midterms are over. Now what?

The arch project is one of several around Washington that the Republican president has undertaken as he alters the capital to his tastes — from renovating one of its storied public golf courses, to threatening to demolish the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. Those projects could soon face intense scrutiny as Democrats will take control of Congress in early January after the results of last week's midterm elections.

The White House last week unveiled a glitzy new website to showcase the arch, which is slated to rise in a mass of gold ornamentation and stately grey granite between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

The family is represented by veteran Washington lawyer Norm Eisen and Democracy Defenders Fund. Eisen and his organization have also filed lawsuits against the Kennedy Center plans and represented a man who successfully fought off prosecution related to an incident at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, after Trump ordered renovations for that Washington, D.C., monument in a no-bid contract.
With files from CBC News

articles.title: Germany news: Only 1/3 of Germans satisfied with state of democracy
articles.summary: A new authoritarianism study has revealed a new low in satisfaction levels with the functioning of German democracy. Meanwhile, the Bundeswehr has banned Chinese-made drones. DW has more.

image.caption: The study also found a high level of chauvinistic and antisemitic tendencies among respondentsImage: James Zabel/Kirchner-Media/IMAGO

blocks.text: November 11, 2026
Satisfaction with democracy in Germany reaches new low — study
Just a third of respondents said they were satisfied with the state of democracy in the Federal Republic of Germany, according to a new report from the Leipzig Authoritarianism Study.

This marked a steep decline from the 42.3% level of satisfaction measured in the last study in 2024 and was the lowest point since the study began in 2002. The level was even lower in the former East German states where only 22.8% expressed satisfaction with German democracy, down from 29.7%.
At the same time, 89.3% of respondents said they agreed with the concept of democracy, however, this also marked the first time this level fell below 90%.
A large share of respondents also expressed chauvinistic and antisemitic views.
In response to the statement "Germany is being dangerously overrun by foreigners," 34.9% were manifestly in agreement, with 24.4% in latent agreement.
At the same time, 15.5% manifestly agreed with the statement "the influence of Jews in Germany is still too great," with 21.7% latently agreeing.
The research was carried out by the Else-Frenkel-Brunswik-Institut at the University of Leipzig. They surveyed 2,500 people between mid-March and the beginning of June this year.

articles.title: Iran classes Argentina navy, air force as 'terrorist organizations'
articles.summary: In a tit-for-tat move, Iran has said it now considers Argentina's navy and air force as "terrorist organizations." Tehran claimed Buenos Aires is responsible for further consequences.

image.caption: Tehran did not mention Argentina's army in the statement [FILE: Mar 19, 2024]Image: Str/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Iran's Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday that it classified Argentina's navy and air force as "terrorist organizations."

In early April, Argentina designated Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a "terrorist organization," as US President Donald Trump pressured his allies to do so following the war on Iran.
Tehran's designation came "based on the principle of reciprocity," Iran's ​Foreign ‌Ministry said in a statement.
All the Ayatollah's men — ensuring the regime's survival
"It is ‌evident ​that the responsibility for all consequences arising from this matter will lie with the Argentine government," the ministry added, ​without a mention of Argentina's army.
Iran passed a legislation in 2019 that grants retaliatory measures against states that designate its military as a terrorist group.
Argentina holds Hezbollah responsible for deadly attacks
Argentina said in April that it had taken action against the IRGC because of its support for the Lebanon-based militant group Hezbollah.

blocks.caption: The 1994 bombing attack that destroyed the AMIA building in Buenos Aires left 85 people deadImage: Daniel Luna/dpa/picture-alliance

blocks.text: Buenos Aires holds Hezbollah responsible for the 1994 bombing of the AMIA Jewish community center, which killed 85 people.
IRGC classified as a terrorist group by many countries
IRGC was established at the end of Iran's 1979 Islamic Revolution as an elite armed militia whose role was to protect the then embryonic Shiite clerical regime.
Over the years, it has morphed into a vast economic and political empire. Rather than the elected president, the force answers directly to Iran's supreme leader.
The United States, the European Union, and the United Kingdom, along with other countries, classify the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as a terrorist organization.

MANILA, Philippines – Summit Media has taken full ownership of entertainment and lifestyle news website PEP.ph and sports publication SPIN.ph, the digital media and publishing company announced on Wednesday, November 11.

PEP.ph was founded in 2006 by editor-in-chief Jo-Ann Maglipon. It has since served as a portal into the lives of Filipino celebrities through showbiz news and blind items. It also publishes content on beauty, finance, and other entertainment-adjacent topics.
PEP.ph, which stands for Philippine Entertainment Portal, was jointly launched by Summit Media and GMA in 2007.

Meanwhile, SPIN.ph, which stands for Sports Interactive Network, was launched in 2012 under a joint partnership between Summit Media and GMA. Its coverage spans anything and everything sports — from tennis to esports to leagues like the PBA, PVL, UAAP, and the NCAA, among others. It is helmed by editor-in-chief Eduardo Catacutan Jr.

“These brands have built something that cannot easily be replicated: credibility, audience relationships, and a deep understanding of Filipino popular culture. Our next chapter is about building on those strengths and expanding the ways audiences experience entertainment,” Summit Media president and CEO Howard Go said in a press release.

This comes just after Summit Media formed a partnership with PlayTime Entertainment in the form of a venture called PT Summit. It aims to use technology to distribute content, engage audiences, and come up with new models in the evolving media ecosystem.

“Our focus is on building capabilities that allow established content businesses to evolve, reach audiences in new ways, and explore opportunities that were previously difficult to pursue. This partnership is about creating the foundation for what comes next,” said Crisanto Roy Alcid, president and CEO of PT Summit.

Amid Summit Media’s move to take full ownership of the two publications, PEP.ph and SPIN.ph will still be able to maintain their editorial voices and exercise their own journalistic standards as they operate daily. – Rappler.com

articles.title: GOP branded ‘sinking ship’ as Republicans block efforts to impeach Hegseth – US politics live
articles.summary: Trump hails ‘exoneration of a Great American Patriot’ as moves against his defense secretary fail for now

blocks.text: Key events

items: 15m agoGOP branded 'sinking ship' as House Republicans block efforts to impeach Hegseth

blocks.text: GOP branded 'sinking ship' as House Republicans block efforts to impeach Hegseth
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
Republican representative Thomas Massie compared the GOP with passengers content to go down with the Titanic after colleagues thwarted his effort to impeach defense secretary Pete Hegseth.

The vote came a week after Republicans lost control of the Senate and House of Representatives in their worst midterm election in more than a half century, and underscored how lawmakers remain wary of crossing Donald Trump, who has signaled his continued support for Hegseth.
“They know it’s a sinking ship but committed to stay on board,” Massie, a Republican congressman who lost his primary after breaking with the president, said.

Top Democrats announced their support for the resolution, but Republicans moved to kill it by referring it to the judiciary committee. Their motion succeeded on Tuesday, by a 211-204 vote, largely along party lines. Massie was the sole Republican to oppose the motion, along with all Democrats.
Trump, who was twice impeached, celebrated what he hailed as the “EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot” and lashed out at Massie for forcing the vote.
“The Democrats continue to weaponize and abuse the United States of America,” Trump said on Truth Social. “They must be stopped!”

The Pentagon, meanwhile, declared “total victory”. “The referral of these baseless impeachment articles to the House judiciary committee marks total victory for Secretary Hegseth, the Department of War, and the American warfighter,” Sean Parnell, a department spokesperson, wrote in a social media post.
Some 11 Democratic representatives skipped the vote, the Daily Beast reported earlier this morning, causing the articles of impeachment to fail. Among those to miss the vote was Nancy Pelosi.
If eight of ‌them had voted with fellow Democrats the measure could have proceeded.

House Democratic leader Hakeen Jeffries said he would talk to members about whether to mount a new impeachment effort in the next ​Congress in January when the Democrats who triumphed in the midterm take their seats. “We’ll have that conversation at the appropriate time,” he said.
Read the full story here:
In other developments:

items: Congressman Jim Jordan, a Republican hardliner from Ohio, won the election to become the next House minority leader in Congress. Jordan beat Representative Steve Scalise, the current majority leader, by 106-73 in a closed-door vote to lead Republicans from January. He replaces the current House speaker, Mike Jonson, who said he would not run when the GOP cedes control to Democrats in the new year.

Meanwhile, Republicans in the upper chamber, re-elected John Thune to serve as Senate minority leader in the next Congress. The GOP senator from North Dakota didn’t face a challenger in the closed-door vote, as Democrats prepare for at least a 10-seat majority in the new year.

Nine members of the Kennedy family sued the Trump administration in an effort to block its construction of a 250-foot triumphal arch. The family’s complaint states that the arch, which is planned for near Arlington national cemetery, would obstruct the Kennedy gravesites, the JFK Eternal Flame and the sightlines of the cemetery, “permanently diminishing these memorials.”

A federal judge has allowed Donald Trump’s defamation lawsuit against the BBC to proceed. Trump is suing Britain’s publicly funded broadcaster for $10bn over an edited clip that made it appear that Trump told his supporters to storm the US Capitol on 6 January 2021.

articles.title: VP Sara earned profits from GenCorp., says firm's counsel
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte earned profit from her investment in GenCorp. Industries, Inc., a defense witness at the impeachment trial said Wednesday.

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 7:01pm
Vice President Sara Duterte earned profit from her investment in GenCorp. Industries, Inc., a defense witness at the impeachment trial said Wednesday.

Attorney Suzette Balucanag-Punay, the in-house counsel of Gencorp Industries, Inc. and Metro City Chow Foods Corporation, made the testimony when asked by Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros about Punay’s testimony of the Vice President receiving P2.14 million return of capital from from Gencorp Industries, Inc. from 2022 to 2025.

Punay also testified that Duterte has a “loose investment” in GenCorp. because sheinvested in Davao Bounty Times Food Corporation before the actual commencement of operations of Jollibee Times Square branch.
Punay said that the Jollibee Times Square branch eventually opened under the franchise granted to Great Jolly Times Foods Corporation, an entity which eventually became Gencorp Industries, Inc.
“This [P2.14 million] is return of capital. So, kumita nga siya [Duterte],” Hontiveros asked.
“Yes,” Punay replied.
Hontiveros asked if this means that the Vice President has financial interest in GenCorp., to which Punay again answered in the affirmative.
But when asked by Hontiveros if the Vice President receiving this payout violates the Constiution, Punay replied she was not sure.
Hontiveros pressed her, asking if the Constitution clearly prohibits an incumbent Vice President from having direct and indirect participation in any business.
Punay, this time, gave a categorical answer.
“Yes, it is in the Constitution, your honor,” she said.

Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan also raised the point of the Vice President's earning profits from GenCorp., noting that Punay initially said during the direct examination the Duterte had zero business participation with GenCorp.

“During the direct examination, you were certain that the Vice President has no participation in GenCorp., zero participation, no stock holdings, she has no position. And then you mentioned that she actually had a loose investment, and she was receiving benefits from that loose investment,” Pangilinan said.
He said Punay's pronouncement, therefore, is inaccurate, given that by receiving payouts, the Vice President is clearly involved in GenCorp.

“It is not correct to say that there is no participation [on the part of the Vice President] or no role whatsoever. You [Vice President]) participated as a beneficiary,” Pangilinan, a lawyer like Punay, added.

Duterte’s 2024 and 2025 Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) that she jointly filed with her husband, Manases Carpio—presented as evidence of the prosecution—earlier showed that Gencorp Industries Inc., formerly known as Timesquare Bee Foods Corp. and Great Jolly Times Food, is one of her business interests.

The Vice President also listed Gencorp Industries Inc.’s former name, Timesquare Bee Foods Corp., as one of her business interests in her 2022 and 2023 SALNs that the prosecution presented as evidence.

The defense is presenting its evidence against Article 2 which accuses the Vice President of betrayal of public trust and culpable violation of the Constitution due to amassing P817 million to P1.5 billion of unexplained wealth due to non-declaration of assets and non-divestment in businesses despite a Constitutional ban. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Merchants can scan unified digital PWD cards for verification --NCDA
articles.summary: The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA) said that merchants can scan the newly established unified digital ID to verify its authenticity. However, it stressed that a presumption of…

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 6:11pm

The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA) said that merchants can scan the newly established unified digital ID to verify its authenticity. However, it stressed that a presumption of regularity should still apply to persons with disabilities (PWD).

The NCDA is rolling out its Unified PWD Identification System (UPWDIS), which is a centralized platform to curb fraudulent PWD cards. The Department of Justice had previously raised the alarm on an estimated 6 million fake PWD cards.

“Ang digital ID natin may unique QR Code po. So, iyong QR code po ii-scan lang ng ating mga merchants and then pag-scan didiretso po iyan sa government portal ng DSWD (Department of Social Welfare and Development), and then makikita po na verified iyong ating persons with disabilities. So ganoon lang kabilis po iyong pag-verify niya,” NCDA spokesperson Walter Jason Alava said on the Bagong Pilipinas Ngayon public briefing.

(Our digital ID has a unique QR code. So, this QR code can be scanned by merchants, which will go directly to a portal of the DSWD, then we can see the verified persons with disabilities. This makes it fast to verify.)
However, Alvava said that there is a Department of Justice (DOJ) opinion that stated that there should be a presumption of regularity

“Mayroon presumption of regularity kapag nag-present po ang ating mga person with disability ng kanilang identification. So, kailangan po bigyan natin sila ng discounts and then, kung nagdududa tayo ‘di ba na iyong person with disability, doon lang tayo magbi-verify,” the spokesperson said.

(There is a presumption of regularity if a person with disabilities presents identification. So we need to give them the discounts and then if we doubt the person with disability, that is when we verify.)
Alvava said that registration for the new digital ID is still in-person at local government units, as the council was still checking how to enhance an online registration system.
According to a Facebook post from the NCDA, a physical card may be printed upon request.

People with existing PWD cards only need to bring their IDs as long as they are still valid and unexpired. For first-time registrants, those who do not have an apparent disability must bring a certificate of disability from a licensed physician. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Sara Duterte received ‘return of capital’ of 2.14 million from GenCorp. — witness
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte has received a “return of capital” from a corporation tied to her, according to the fourth witness of the defense panel.

blocks.text: November 11, 2026 | 6:08pm
MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte has received a “return of capital” from a corporation tied to her, according to the fourth witness of the defense panel.

In her testimony, lawyer Suzette Balucanag-Punay, the in-house counsel of two corporations tied to the vice president, said that Duterte received a “return of capital” from GenCorp Industries Inc. from 2022 to 2025, amounting to P2.14 million.
According to Punay, citing company records, Duterte received disbursements of P555,750 in 2023, P612,419.14 in 2024 and P636,700 in 2025.
She also said that these disbursements were made through checks issued from a bank account belonging to Jollibee Times Square, which is tied to GenCorp.
Punay described the Vice President's financial interest as a "loose investment" tied specifically to a single branch, Jollibee Times Square, rather than equity in GenCorp itself.
“Even in Times Square branch, she has no involvement or participation,” Punay said.
Punay also said that Duterte has not received any dividends from the corporation, as it did not declare any.

Prosecution evidence shows that Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, listed GenCorp Industries Inc., previously named Timesquare Bee Foods Corp. and Great Jolly Times Food, as a business interest in their joint SALNs for 2024 and 2025, as well as under its former name in her 2022 and 2023 filings.

Meanwhile, her brother, Davao City Mayor Sebastian "Baste" Duterte, testified before the impeachment court that while the city government awarded P33 million in contracts to GenCorp, he was unaware of his sister's connection to the company.

Article 7, Section 13 of the 1987 Constitution provides that the president, vice president, members of the Cabinet and their deputies or assistants shall not “hold any other office or employment during their tenure,” in order to avoid conflicts of interest.

It also prohibits these officials, during their tenure, from “directly or indirectly, practice any other profession, participate in any business, or be financially interested in any contract with, or in any franchise, or special privilege granted by the Government or any subdivision, agency, or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries.”
Franchise history
Punay traced the history back to 2007, when Duterte was a stockholder in Davao Bounty Times Food Corp., according to her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth.
She explained that Davao Bounty was originally incorporated to operate the Jollibee Times Square branch but failed to secure the franchise.
The franchise was instead granted to Great Jolly Times Foods Corporation, and Duterte's original investment was carried over.
Through a series of corporate transitions, the operations of the Times Square branch were eventually absorbed by GenCorp.
Punay asserted that because the original venture did not operate, the money being paid to Duterte is simply the return of her initial capital.
45 times higher

Senate Presiding Officer Francis Escudero pointed out that Duterte received P2.14 million from GenCorp between 2022 and 2025, about 45 times her documented P46,875 capital contribution to Davao Bounty Foods Corporation.
During the hearing, Escudero explained the difference between a return of investment and a return on investment.
Punay admitted that she could not explain how the payouts reached P2.14 million or point to additional investments justifying the total.
She eventually agreed with defense lawyer Lorna Kapunan that the sum represented earnings either way.
“Whether it be a return on investment or a return of investment, it is still income, correct?” Kapunan asked. To which Punay replied: “Yes.”
Punay is the fourth defense witness in Duterte’s impeachment trial under Article II of the Articles of Impeachment.
Article II covers allegations involving Duterte's alleged ill-gotten wealth and failure to fully disclose her assets and liabilities in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth.

articles.title: [Be The Good] Let’s not rely on Leni Robredo
articles.summary: When we look to one person, we miss the opportunity to cultivate a wider selection of politicians

blocks.text: She has spoken. The ship has sailed. Those hoping Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo would run for a national post in 2028 got a reality check on Monday, November 9. This whole fixation on Mayor Robredo though also got me thinking of a related issue: the shallow bench for alternative candidates.

When we look to one person, we miss the opportunity to cultivate a wider selection of politicians. Perhaps this decision of Robredo’s is a chance to widen our horizons and look to new faces. More importantly, it should allow us to examine ourselves. Quoting Mahatma Gandhi, should we not become the change we want to see?

I just came from a week in Cape Town, South Africa with Rappler’s scholars to the One Young World 2026 Summit. JJ Agustin, Gybel Agregado, Kit Posadas, John Mauro Manuel, and Jasser Mohammad are examples of young people who are becoming the change they want to see. They live it every day, in their work in youth political participation, agriculture, women empowerment, and data-driven storytelling. At the summit, which gathered 2,000 young people from over 190 countries, we listened to fellow youth leaders tell stories of the hardships they overcame, the challenges they continue to face, and the hope they keep alive for their communities and countries.
One speech at the summit resonated with me – that of Anna Strolenberg, who, at 31 years old, is one of the youngest members of the European Parliament.
Anna was recognized as one of the Politicians of the Year, an award given out at every One Young World Summit.
Like most of us, she used to think politics was a dirty word, “something for men with big egos and bad suits.”
But, when she was 24 years old, she decided to become a politician, not because she thought she’d be good at political maneuverings, but simply because she was fed up with the status quo.

“Many of you told me you have lost trust in politics because politicians are corrupt, or don’t represent you. And I want to tell you this: do not accept it. Go there yourself and make them change,” she said, to resounding applause.

I know many Filipinos don’t trust politics. Most of us are cynical, or have lost hope and have simply checked out. I get it. The headlines scream with reasons to be jaded: the massive flood control corruption, the poor services and facilities, the red tape and incompetence, the grandstanding with nothing to show for it. We rail against these failures of governance all the time. We are adept at outrage. If dissatisfaction with the status quo was a marathon, we would’ve won it a thousand times over.
But Anna said this cannot be enough.

“I have a warning, because our passion for protest doesn’t translate to a passion for politics. Young people have the most to gain, but by not being present, we accept that other people put us last,” she said.

Anna refused to accept this. Not even 30 years old, she set aside her nerves and doubts, and decided to join Volt Europa, a political party. The story of Volt is in itself striking. It was founded by three young people who met while studying at Columbia University and who decided they wanted to create a truly pan-European progressive political party that would push back against the nationalist, right-wing movements gaining ground in the region.
That was in 2017. Today, Volt has over 30,000 members from all over Europe, 400 members elected into office, including five in the European Parliament. Anna is one of those five.

“I know that politics is often a dirty word, but I think it’s up to us to change it. I am proud to say I’m a member of the European Parliament, that I’m changing politics – step by step, but I’m changing it,” said Anna at the One Young World Summit.

All over the world, we are seeing young people stepping out of their comfort zones, and getting some power in return. From France, to Nepal, to Bangladesh, to Serbia, youth-led protests and movements have sparked change, replaced regimes, or at the very least, catalyzed urgent conversations.

In the US, the youth vote played a decisive role in the blue wave that has given back power to the Democrats. Some 66% of voters aged 18 to 29 voted for Democratic candidates for the House of Representatives.

For sure, it is a difficult, even dangerous, road to take back power. In the Philippines, the electoral system is such that massive resources are needed to run for public office. But people with extremely limited resources can change the fate of a nation. South Africa gives us the best example. Nelson Mandela and his fellow freedom fighters against apartheid were facing deadly state force and next to no funding, not to mention a whole ecosystem of discriminatory laws, yet still managed to bring down the repressive system. It came at a great cost. But it was a cost they took on because the dream was worth it.
What dream for the Philippines is worth the cost? What cost are you willing to pay?

You can start by registering to vote in the 2028 elections, if you haven’t yet. Voter registration resumed on Monday, November 10 and will continue until July 30, 2027. You can register to vote at any Comelec office and certain malls, from 8 am to 5 pm. Here’s the directory of Comelec offices nationwide.

articles.title: Stellantis auto plant sale draws optimism, hurt in Brampton, Ont., after 2,000 jobs lost
articles.summary: Workers and local politicians are expressing disappointment at Stellantis's decision to sell its Brampton, Ont., plant to armoured vehicle maker Roshel Inc., but some local businesses and experts say…

image.caption: The Stellantis assembly plant in Brampton, Ont., has been purchased by Canadian armoured vehicle maker Roshel Inc. following a three-year shutdown, rattling autoworkers who lost their jobs. (Patrick Morrell/CBC)

blocks.text: Toronto·New

Workers and local politicians are expressing disappointment at Stellantis's decision to sell its Brampton, Ont., plant to armoured vehicle maker Roshel Inc., but some local businesses and experts say the new company could bring more jobs and foot traffic to the community.
Brampton Board of Trade hopes new owner means new jobs, investment, more local business
For three years, Shelly Lewis has been trying to increase foot traffic at her restaurant after it dwindled following the 2023 closure of the Stellantis auto plant in Brampton, Ont.

Shelly's Kitchen on Chrysler Drive is among the many food shops that relied on business from thousands of Stellantis workers, but Lewis said she's had to lay off a staff member and admits she has struggled to pay bills some months.
"The Stellantis plant made business for me because I had staff at all hours come in and I had lots of specials," she said. "I'm so sad that they shut down operations."
Now, however, she's hopeful that news the automater is expected to have a new owner will result in more customers at her eatery and rejuvenate the area.
On Monday, it was announced that Canadian armoured ⁠vehicle maker Roshel Inc. will buy the auto plant, acquiring the idled facility and equipment from Stellantis for an undisclosed amount.

items: Roshel to buy Stellantis assembly plant in Brampton for undisclosed amount, automaker says

blocks.text: That appears to be positive news, as more than 2,000 workers were laid off when operations were halted in in 2023 to retool the plant for Jeep production, a plan that was paused in early 2025.

Baltej Bajwa, among the over 2,000 workers laid off from Brampton's Stellantis facility, says it's great that Roshel is offering jobs to workers in the city, but fears there will be lots of uncertainty for colleagues. (CBC)
But Baltej Bajwa, one of the laid-off workers who's been left in limbo since the plant's closure, remains uncertain of his future and said he was shocked to hear about the sale.
"Any hope that we had of potentially coming back when we heard the news kind of just got shattered," Bajwa said.

items: How Pearson airport plans to fill jobs with laid-off Stellantis workers

blocks.text: Roshel Inc. CEO Roman Shimonov did say the company plans to employ thousands of people and will give first priority to the workers who lost their job in Brampton.
However, Bajwa said, Roshel's production capacity will be far fewer than the 400 to 800 vehicles that the 2,200 Stellantis workers produced daily.

"So yes, it's amazing that Roshel is giving us those job opportunities, but it still does kind of leave the other half of the plant in a state of disarray where we don't know where we're going to go."
'They can't cut and run,' mayor says
Roshel's purchase of the plant has garnered harsh words from union leaders and politicians.
Prime Minister Mark Carney called it a "betrayal" to all Canadians.
Lana Payne, national president of Unifor, said Monday that the sale is an "unacceptable outcome" for the union and its members, calling it the "worst-case scenario."

items: Stellantis auto plant closure in Brampton a 'betrayal' to all Canadians, Carney says

blocks.text: Brampton Mayor Patrick Brown echoed those sentiments. He said Stellantis has received "bailouts" from various levels of government over the years, including most recently in 2022, "on the basis of production in Canada."

"Brampton residents are rightfully angry. I think Canadians should be angry," he told CBC News on Tuesday. "This is a company that has depended on Canadian taxpayer generosity for decades. They can't cut and run without consequences.

"Stellantis has abandoned Canadian workers — they got bullied by the Trump administration. If we allow Stellantis to leave easily and ignore their legal obligations, this will not be the last auto plant that falls in Canada. Really, this is ground zero of protecting auto jobs."
In a statement, Stellantis said it would voluntarily repay the subsidies.
Purchase will drive up economic activity: Board of Trade
Brown said he thinks Roshel is a great local company that has ambitions to create thousands of jobs, but doesn't believe it should have purchased Stellantis.
However, Jaipaul Massey-Singh, CEO of the Brampton Board of Trade, believes this will be a boon to the city and the local economy.

He said the impact of Stellantis's closure goes beyond just workers, affecting their families and the local businesses they were supporting. He has heard from many shops that have laid off staff, lost orders and reduced their hours to stay afloat.

"Knowing that it's going to result in activity in that plant once more, creating employment for those who are going to be there but also additional employment and economic activity for the community in general, is absolutely welcome news," Massey-Singh said about the sale.

"For every employee that's affected, it's up to, five to six additional employees or workers in that community that are impacted. So in a place like Brampton, we're talking minimum [12,000] to 15,000 individuals who were impacted by Stellantis's decision to walk away."

The Chrysler Brampton Assembly plant is seen Nov. 10 in this image taken by drone. Local leaders have condemned Stellantis's decision to sell the plant, leaving over 2,000 workers without jobs. However, local businesses hope the sale will bring more foot traffic to the area. (Patrick Morrell/CBC)

Massey-Singh hopes every laid-off Stellantis employee gets their jobs back, and believes reopening the plant under new ownership will drive more investment and business in the form of new workers, retraining and additional resources.
Lewis remains optimistic that Roshel joining the community will help boost business for her restaurant and other local establishments.
"I'm happy that something else will be there again because they'll have people working there again and this plaza has lots of different businesses, so I know it's going to be better for everybody."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Isha Bhargava is a multiplatform reporter for CBC News in Peel Region where she covers everything from local news to current affairs and human interest stories. She was previously with CBC London. You can reach out to her with your story ideas at isha.bhargava@cbc.ca
With files from Dana Roberts, CBC News

articles.title: N.B. veteran to wear replica medals on Remembrance Day after originals were stolen
articles.summary: A 91-year-old New Brunswick veteran thought he might have to spend this Remembrance Day without his medals after his were stolen from his home this summer. But that won't be the case for retired…

image.caption: Retired lieutenant-colonel Alan Kennedy, 91, will wear a set of replica medals this Remembrance Day after his original set was stolen from his home in July. (Aniekan Etuhube/CBC)

blocks.text: New Brunswick

A 91-year-old New Brunswick veteran thought he might have to spend this Remembrance Day without his medals after his were stolen from his home this summer. But that won't be the case for retired lieutenant-colonel Alan Kennedy. While they aren't the originals, the replicas, made possible because of the effort of a fellow veteran and kindness of a local businesswoman, will be pinned over his heart on Nov. 11.
Retired lieutenant-colonel Alan Kennedy had his medals taken from his home earlier this year
A 91-year-old New Brunswick veteran thought he might have to spend this Remembrance Day without his medals after they were stolen from his home this summer.
But that won't be the case for retired lieutenant-colonel Alan Kennedy.
While they aren't the originals, the replicas — made possible by the effort of a fellow veteran and kindness of a local business owner — will be pinned over his heart on Nov. 11.
David Hughes, a retired captain and now the manager of the New Brunswick Military History Museum, arranged to have the set made.
"For a soldier to not have his medals on Remembrance Day, that's a stab in the heart," Hughes said.
Hughes said soldiers identify as such for their whole lives, whether they're serving or not.
91-year-old veteran given replica medals after originals stolen
Kennedy was a soldier for his entire adult life, and so were his friends.

His original medals were stolen on July 9, when three people broke into his home in Nasonworth. He said the individuals tied him to a chair with zip ties and took off with a large sum of money and many of his military keepsakes, including his medals.

The RCMP West District community crime reduction unit is still seeking information about the home invasion. The suspects are described as two men and a woman, all tall and thin, wearing face coverings.
Kennedy said his house is full of things he had collected from travelling around the world.
"I wasn't frightened as such," he said. "I was very concerned that they were taking things I had."
Alan Kennedy, left, received his replacement medals from David Hughes of the New Brunswick Military History Museum. (Submitted by David Hughes)

When Hughes learned what happened, helping Kennedy became his mission. When he found out official replacements from the military would be a long process and Remembrance Day was fast approaching, he looked to a local business for help.
Hughes went to see Michela Amato at Michela's Medal Mounting in Oromocto and started telling her what had happened.
Amato told Hughes she had already heard about Kennedy's story, Hughes recalled, and she offered to make the replica set free of charge.
"Just great kindness and humanity on her part," Hughes said.
The medals were finished a couple of weeks ago and Hughes presented them to Kennedy in front of some of his veteran friends.
"It was the one little thing that I could do for him," Hughes said. "It felt really good."
Kennedy said the replicas “look exactly like the real ones.”

The replica set made for Alan Kennedy includes the officer of the Order of Military Merit and the Canadian Forces' Decoration with two clasps for 32 years of service. (Submitted by New Brunswick Military History Museum)

The set reflects a career that began in the artillery and took him through the Black Watch, one of Canada's oldest and most distinguished infantry regiments, along with the Royal Canadian Regiment and the Canadian Airborne Regiment.

The set includes his officer of the Order of Military Merit, a medal for his two tours of Cyprus, a United Nations medal for his time as a military observer in India and Pakistan, and his Canadian Forces' Decoration with two bars for 32 years of service.
Kennedy has worn his medals every Remembrance Day for years and this year will be no exception.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Polina Kozlova is a journalist based in Fredericton. You can contact her with story ideas at polina.kozlova@cbc.ca .

articles.title: Why the first U-boat to surrender in North America landed in this N.S. town
articles.summary: Speaking through an interpreter, the U-boat's commander said he would 'very much' like to stay in Canada or the U.S.

image.caption: Some of the German crew members from U-889 are shown after surrendering to the Allies on May 13, 1945, in Shelburne, N.S. (CWM 20070014-016/George Metcalf Archival Collection/Canadian War Museum)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia·New
Speaking through an interpreter, the U-boat's commander said he would 'very much' like to stay in Canada or the U.S.
The U-boat was analyzed by Canadian officials to understand what equipment was on board

After Germany's unconditional surrender in May 1945 during the Second World War, German submarines known as U-boats were ordered to surrender, but whether the crews would comply was a question that worried Allied commanders.

U-boats were to head to the surface of whatever waters they were in and fly a black flag to indicate they were obeying and would not fight anymore. They would then surrender to Allied forces at sea, before being escorted to port.
While the war in Europe was over, it was still ongoing in the Pacific.
"It's a pretty grave concern on the part of Allied commanders, which is what threat do they pose?" said Jeff Noakes, the Second World War historian with the Canadian War Museum.
"And also, are they even going to surrender? Because there is a worry that there might be diehard German submarine commanders who don't want to give up and who might want to keep on fighting."
For U-boats in the Atlantic, most surrendered on the European side, said Noakes.
For ones on the western side, there were four North American ports they could surrender to, with the first landing in Shelburne, N.S., where a throng of reporters interviewed the ship's captain.
A Royal Canadian Navy seaman is shown with the White Ensign on board U-889 on May 13, 1945. (CWM 20070014-017/George Metcalf Archival Collection/Canadian War Museum)
Noakes said the metric the Royal Canadian Navy used in labelling Shelburne as the first was when a surrendered U-boat arrived at a North American port.
"There may well have been other U-boats in the western part of the Atlantic that surrendered to Allied forces, or at least were spotted by Allied forces sooner," said Noakes.
Besides Shelburne, the other ports where U-boats could surrender in North America were in Bay Bulls, Dominion of Newfoundland (which had not yet joined Canada), and two in the United States.
Part of a Second World War Allied document shows the co-ordinates for ports where the Royal Canadian Navy said German U-boats could surrender. (Submitted by Derek Waller)
U-boats were not named, but were numbered. Before U-889 and its crew of around 55 landed in Shelburne on May 13, 1945, a surrender ceremony was held just offshore.

Witnessing the Shelburne ceremony were Royal Canadian Navy officials, "a flotilla of Royal Canadian Navy families and Royal Navy frigates, a squadron of [Royal Canadian Air Force] planes and a group of approximately 35 newspapermen," The Toronto Telegram reported in its May 14, 1945, edition.

items: Family lore said my grandfather's WW II ship was torpedoed. The truth was far more interesting
Sinking of HMCS Otter in WW II Halifax remembered as 'dramatic tale of tension and heroics'

blocks.text: Noakes said there was tremendous symbolic importance attached to these events.
U-889 departed Norway on its maiden voyage in April 1945 and was on its way to New York. The plan was to sit at the harbour's entrance to attack ships, but the surrender order scuttled those plans.
The signing of the unconditional surrender of German armed forces of the Third Reich happened on May 7, 1945, at the Allied headquarters in Reims, eastern France. (AFP via Getty Images)
It was spotted by a Royal Canadian Navy plane on May 10, 1945, off Newfoundland. Canadian vessels then escorted U-889 to Shelburne.
In Shelburne, the U-boat's commander, Friedrich Braeucker, gave an interview to the press.
Noakes called this pretty unusual.
The May 14, 1945, Toronto Telegram included images of a crew member from U-889, left, and the ship's captain, Friedrich Braeucker. (www.newspapers.com)

"You're now interviewing [the] commander and other personnel from a German submarine that … just over a week before would technically have been in a position, you know, to be attacking Canadian warships," he said.

When Braeucker was asked about the persecution of Jewish people and others in Germany and German-occupied countries, he called it "a beastly, brutal thing. I do not believe in it," The Toronto Telegram reported.

items: This Nova Scotian's dad flew a Spitfire during WW II. He just went to Poland to see it
Why some Allied troops fighting in WW II were dubbed D-Day Dodgers

blocks.text: The paper described the 26-year-old as slight and handsome with brown hair.
Speaking through an interpreter, he said he would "very much" like to stay in Canada or the U.S.
Braeucker was also asked if he could accept living in a democracy.
"There is not such a big difference between your government and ours," he said with a shrug, The Canadian Press reported.
The crew members from U-889 are shown being brought ashore to Shelburne on a Royal Canadian Navy vessel. (CWM 20070014-016/George Metcalf Archival Collection/Canadian War Museum)
Most of U-889's crew members were in their early 20s, with the youngest crew member being 19 and the oldest 33, and they were "a chubby-faced, shaggy-haired lot," reported The Toronto Telegram.

After its stay in Shelburne, U-889 was led by a Canadian warship and then taken to Halifax, arriving on May 24, 1945. A story in The Windsor Star noted that "shortly afterward, a string of Allied merchant ships, once the hunted quarry, followed in line into port."
Noakes said the U-boat was analyzed by Canadian officials to understand what equipment was on board and the technology it had.

items: When the Americans landed at Omaha Beach on D-Day, they had help from Halifax
Why astronomy played a pivotal role in setting D-Day date
The ghost's warm hands that spared a brother's life at Vimy

blocks.text: By summer and into the fall, U-889 and U-190 — which surrendered in Newfoundland, a day after U-889 arrived in Shelburne — were escorted by Canadian warships and taken to East Coast ports on publicity tours.
"This is partly to show to people this is what the enemy had," said Noakes. "It's also being done as fundraising."
American ports

All told, five U-boats ended up in American ports, said Derek Waller, the author of The Surrender of the U-Boat Fleet 1945. He told CBC News in an email that four of the U-boats landed in Portsmouth, N.H., and the fifth was taken to Fort Miles, Del.

"In the end the surrender process in the Western Atlantic proved to be very easy — primarily because of the lack of U-boats still in the area," he said in an email. "But the naval planners did not know that before the capitulation actually took place."
U-889 was later transferred to the United States Navy and was sunk off its coast in November 1947.

articles.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading
articles.summary: The latest health ministry data Wednesday showed 11,042 people have been infected by the deadly virus that has now killed 5,387, nearly half of those infected, in the country's deadliest outbreak.

image.caption: A healthcare worker walks inside an Ebola treatment center in Beni, North Kivu Province, Congo, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. (Sebastien Kitsa Musayi/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Health·New
The latest health ministry data Wednesday showed 11,042 people have been infected by the deadly virus that has now killed 5,387, nearly half of those infected, in the country's deadliest outbreak.
The Bundibugyo virus responsible for this outbreak has no known vaccine or treatment

Congo's Ebola outbreak has topped 11,000 cases, the government said Wednesday, a stark figure that underscores the severity of the situation as the country grapples with the relentless spread of the disease.

According to the latest health ministry data, 11,042 people have been infected with the deadly virus that has now killed 5,387 — nearly half of those infected in what has been Congo's deadliest outbreak.

items: 'No one is safe' as Ebola outbreak surges to more than 10,000 cases, Africa's top doctor warns Canada

blocks.text: The outbreak was declared in mid-May, and since then, Congolese authorities have struggled to contain it due to several factors, including armed conflicts, a health system crisis, poor roads and violence from residents fueled by mistrust and misinformation.
The Bundibugyo virus responsible for this outbreak has no known vaccine or treatment and has spread to eight of the country's 26 provinces.
What Canadians should know about the Ebola outbreak

The resurgence of violence in the two major hotspots in Ituri and North Kivu provinces has sparked worry among health authorities who are calling for a halt to the fighting to allow health workers unhindered access to the sick.

items: Nigeria Ebola patient flown to Switzerland, Congo health worker killed as 4 countries deal with outbreak

blocks.text: Health facilities and medical professionals have also been targeted by many in communities skeptical of the virus, and there have been several attacks on health workers.
Experts have called for more efforts to slow and contain the disease in Congo, while it has spread to multiple African countries including Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria.

Dozens of Ebola outbreaks have been reported since the disease was first discovered in 1976. The largest and deadliest occurred in West Africa in 2014 to 2016, with 28,000 infections and more than 11,000 deaths.
The current outbreak already ranks second and has had at least three times the number of cases and deaths in the time since it was declared, compared with the West Africa outbreak.
